$comment: Full v0.1 scope. Agents may only change `passes` (after the feature's steps pass end to end) and append to `notes`. Adding, removing or rewording entries needs the maintainer (PR label `scope-change`). Order within a milestone is priority order. See ADR 0012.

features.description: Scaffold the pnpm monorepo per ADR 0003 with strict TypeScript, Biome, Vitest and dependency-cruiser; `pnpm check` runs typecheck, lint, unit tests and architecture rules.
steps: Fresh clone: `pnpm install && pnpm check` exits 0
Add a fixture import from `apps/web` into `packages/lang-2610`: `pnpm check` fails and the message names the rule and the allowed alternative
Each package has `src/`, `test/`, and a README of at most 10 lines stating its responsibility
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-21: fresh clone `pnpm install && pnpm check` exits 0; `pnpm test -t F-001` and `-t ADR-0003` cover steps 2 and 3. No e2e harness exists before F-002/F-003.

features.description: Minimal web app (header plus three empty columns) that builds with Vite and deploys to Netlify from `main` via `netlify.toml`.
steps: `pnpm dev` serves the app locally; the header shows the app name
`netlify.toml` at the repo root sets the build command, publish directory, Node and pnpm versions, the QA-30 security headers and a single-page-app fallback
Merging to `main` deploys to https://nf-builder.netlify.app and the page loads; a pull request gets a deploy preview
The deployed page sends a Content-Security-Policy header that matches QA-30
features.notes: App name: nf-builder (Q1). Netlify site `nf-builder` already exists and deploys from this repo's `main`. Verified 2026-11-21: `pnpm test:e2e -- --grep F-002` (6 tests) and unit tests; deploy-check on PR #3 confirmed the preview's headers. Step 3's production half is confirmed by deploy-check on the push to `main` (Q11).

features.description: CI on every PR: `pnpm check`, Playwright smoke on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, bundle-size budget, network host allow-list check, ADR lint, features.json validation.
steps: A PR shows all jobs
Deliberately breaking each check in a throwaway branch makes the matching job fail with an actionable message
ADR lint rejects a duplicate number, a missing status line, or an ADR missing from the index
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-21: CI on PR #4 (all jobs green, Firefox and WebKit ran the @smoke test); throwaway PR #5 broke every check and each job failed with its own message; ADR lint step 3 cases in unit tests and on #5. No e2e test of its own: the CI runs are the end-to-end evidence. QA-34 (audit, Renovate) added to the spec list (scope-change, Q12).

features.description: Agent harness: `pnpm smoke` (build plus one e2e test), PR template with definition-of-done checklist, and a features.json guard that rejects changes other than `passes`/`notes` unless the PR has the `scope-change` label.
steps: `pnpm smoke` runs in under 60 s locally
A PR that rewords a feature description fails the guard; the same PR with `scope-change` passes
AGENTS.md commands section matches the real scripts in package.json
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-21: `pnpm smoke` 4.0 s locally, about 5 s in CI; step 2 shown by throwaway PR #9 (Scope guard run 44950863653 failed on the reworded description, run 44950892037 passed after adding scope-change); step 3 by test/agents-md.test.ts. No e2e test of its own, so `--grep F-004` finds nothing; the CI runs are the end-to-end evidence.

features.description: Corpus tooling: `tools/corpus/corpus.yaml` lists pinned pipelines (repo plus tag or SHA); `pnpm corpus:fetch` downloads them into a git-ignored cache; CI caches them.
steps: `pnpm corpus:fetch` fetches nf-core/rnaseq, nf-core/sarek, nf-core/fetchngs, nextflow-io/rnaseq-nf (main and typed branch) at pinned refs
A second run is a no-op
Malformed fixtures live in `tools/corpus/fixtures/` and are committed
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-21: `pnpm corpus:fetch` fetched 5 pins (about 5 s, 63 MB), second run `0 fetched, 5 up to date` with no git call; fixtures' lint results confirmed with nextflow lint 26.10.7; CI `corpus` job on PR #10 (cache miss then hit). No UI, so no Playwright test (Q13).

features.description: Spike S1: run real Nextflow 26.10 in CI on fixture pipelines to settle typed/legacy interop across files, read the `.module-info` format from Nextflow's source, and confirm the latest 26.10 patch.
steps: CI job runs `nextflow lint` and `nextflow run -stub` on: typed workflow calling a legacy process included from another file; legacy workflow calling a typed process; a script mixing both (expected to fail)
Report in `docs/research/` records each outcome with logs
ADR 0007 history and LA-14 updated (via a Proposed ADR if the decision changes)
features.notes: The oracle job should also lint tools/corpus/fixtures/ and check each result against fixtures.yaml (AGENTS.md, ADR 0017). Verified 2026-11-22 on PR #13: the CI oracle job (Temurin 21, cold cache download checked against the pinned SHA-256, nextflow -version 26.10.7) ran nextflow lint and run -stub on eight S1 cases (16 checks) and linted the nine corpus fixtures, all matching; the local run agrees. Report: docs/research/2026-11-22-spike-s1-typed-legacy-interop.md. No Playwright test, so --grep F-005 finds nothing; the CI run is the end-to-end evidence (Q13).

features.description: Spike S2: vendor the 26.10 nf-lang grammars, generate a TypeScript parser with antlr-ng, port the lexer base class, parse the corpus; build `tools/spec-extract` and produce `script.json` and `config.json`.
steps: Report lists parse pass rate per corpus pipeline and the sarek parse time
Every file that `nextflow lint` accepts parses; differences are listed with causes
Catalogue counts of directives, operators and factories match the docs reference pages, or the gaps are explained
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-22: step 1 by pnpm gen:grammar 26.10 --check and the lang-2610 parse tests; step 2 by pnpm test:corpus (570 of 570 lint-accepted corpus files parse; 3 fixture differences listed with causes) in the CI corpus-parse job; step 3 by pnpm gen:catalogue 26.10 --check in the CI catalogue job and the docs-compare table. Report: docs/research/2026-11-22-spike-s2-parser.md. No Playwright test, so --grep F-006 finds nothing (Q13). F-101 steps 2 and 3 are covered by the generator tests (T1, T2).

features.description: Spike S3: run `language-server-all.jar` under CheerpJ in a Web Worker and exchange LSP messages; measure cold start, memory and diagnostics latency. At most three sessions.
steps: A test page sends `initialize` and `textDocument/didOpen` and receives diagnostics for a file with a known error
Report records cold start, peak memory and diagnostics time against the ADR 0010 thresholds
ADR 0010 updated with the outcome

features.description: Spike S4: deploy a probe page to Netlify (a deploy preview is enough) that calls the registry API endpoints, raw.githubusercontent.com and codeload.github.com, and records CORS results.
steps: Probe results (status, CORS headers, timing) are captured by a Playwright run against the deployed page
Registry endpoint paths are verified against https://registry.nextflow.io/openapi/
ADR 0009 updated with the outcome
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-22 on PR #14: S4 probe run 44983841745 against deploy preview #14 (commit dd44cf4) in Chromium 159, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2 recorded status, CORS headers and timing for 16 targets (step 1); the @openapi test matched all 10 registry targets to OpenAPI 0.14.0 (step 2); ADR 0009 spike result appended (step 3). Report: docs/research/2026-11-22-spike-s4-cors.md. pnpm test:e2e -- --grep F-008 runs the two local page tests; the deployed probe runs under e2e/s4-probe.config.ts. Probe kept for re-runs until F-502.

features.description: Spike S5: run nf-metro in a Web Worker under Pyodide (installing it without its native PNG and animation dependencies) and render the nf-core example `.mmd` files to SVG; measure download size and time.
steps: A test page renders two nf-metro example maps to SVG in the browser
The SVG matches the CLI output for the same input (visual diff within tolerance)
Report records download size, first-render time and any nf-metro patches needed; ADR 0013 updated with the outcome

features.description: `packages/lang-2610` parser: generated lexer and parser for scripts and configs, hand-ported base classes, lexer tests ported from upstream nf-lang tests.
steps: `pnpm --filter lang-2610 test` passes, including ported lexer cases
`pnpm gen:grammar 26.10` regenerates byte-identical output
Generated files carry a do-not-edit header naming the upstream commit
features.notes: From F-006: steps 2 and 3 are delivered (generated parser with do-not-edit headers, pnpm gen:grammar --check). nf-lang has no lexer tests, so step 1's ported cases are the parse cases of ScriptAstBuilderTest and ConfigAstBuilderTest (record in open-questions.md when this lands).

features.description: Script AST with source ranges and attached comments for every declaration and statement kind in the 26.10 syntax reference, typed and legacy.
steps: Snapshot tests cover each construct in the syntax reference
Every AST node's range slices back to its exact source text

features.description: Config AST with source ranges and comments: scopes, assignments, selectors, profiles, includeConfig.
steps: Snapshot tests on every corpus `nextflow.config` and `conf/*.config`
Ranges slice back to exact source

features.description: Lossless round trip with declaration-level fallback: a brace-aware pre-scanner splits files so one bad declaration doesn't sink the file; unparseable files are kept verbatim.
steps: Corpus test: parse and print every file with no edits; output is equivalent (spec glossary) for 100% of files
Malformed fixtures: the bad declaration is isolated, the rest of the file is modelled

features.description: Semantic model: resolve includes (relative paths and registry module names), declarations by name, and dependencies between files.
steps: On each corpus pipeline, every include resolves or produces a diagnostic naming the missing path
Changing one file re-models only that file and its dependants (asserted via instrumentation)

features.description: Projection for typed workflows: calls, operator chains, factories, take, emit, params and output nodes, and def-use edges with Channel/Value types.
steps: Snapshot tests on typed fixtures and the typed rnaseq-nf branch
Node identities are stable across a re-parse with whitespace-only changes

features.description: Projection for legacy workflows: `.out` access, pipes, `set`/`tap`, legacy process ports from qualifiers.
steps: Snapshot tests on nf-core/rnaseq, sarek and fetchngs workflows
Report the share of statements modelled per corpus workflow; target at least 90% overall

features.description: Code nodes: unmodellable statements become code nodes with inputs and outputs from free-variable analysis.
steps: Fixtures with arbitrary Groovy statements produce code nodes wired to the right variables
Round trip remains equivalent

features.description: Generated 26.10 catalogue (`script.json`, `config.json`) committed in `lang-2610`, plus `palette.yaml` overlay with a validation test; CI regenerates on dispatch and fails on hand edits.
steps: `palette.yaml` references only names present in the catalogue (test)
Regeneration in CI produces no diff
No legacy-only construct appears in the palette definition
features.notes: From F-006: catalogue/{script,config}.json are generated by pnpm gen:catalogue from the language server v26.10.2 (nf-lang 26.10.4) and checked by the CI catalogue job; F-109 adds palette.yaml and on-demand regeneration. Overloads with different @Description (for example Channel combine) currently give the entry the description of the first overload by signature text; keep per-signature descriptions when the palette needs them.

features.description: Printer for typed declarations (process, workflow, record, function, params, output, include) matching `nextflow lint -format`; oracle job in CI.
steps: Oracle job formats every printer fixture with Nextflow 26.10 and finds no difference
Printed fixtures pass `nextflow lint` with no errors
features.notes: From F-005 (S1): in typed code the printer emits a legacy tuple input as tuple(a, b, ...), one argument per declared component; a mixed list literal fails nextflow lint (LA-14).

features.description: Core edit commands: CreateProcess (own file, flag, include), AddCall, Connect, Disconnect, DeleteNode, RenameDeclaration, ReplaceFileText, with property tests.
steps: fast-check: results parse; declarations outside targets stay equivalent; undo restores exact bytes
CreateProcess writes `modules/local/<name>/main.nf` with `nextflow.enable.types = true` and adds the include
An edit that would mix typed and legacy definitions in one script is refused with a message

features.description: Diagnostics: parser errors, constructs invalid for the language version, deprecations, type mismatches on edges, and suggestions for legacy patterns.
steps: Each lint has a positive and negative fixture
Every message states what to do; mechanical cases carry a quick-fix command

features.description: Engine runs in a Web Worker behind a Comlink API with incremental per-file re-parse; budgets QA-03 and QA-04 measured in CI.
steps: Benchmark job reports sarek parse time and edit p95 against budgets
The main thread does no parsing (asserted in a Playwright performance trace)
features.notes: From F-201's plan: the shell reads installed pack versions through engine on the main thread; once a pack's entry holds the parser, move that list behind the worker so the parser stays out of the initial bundle (QA-01 check will catch it). From F-006: QA-03 risk. Sarek parses in 1.1 s warm but 15.9 s cold in Node (first-use DFA construction for real grammar ambiguities; upstream Java pays it too). Measure in the worker, then consider parsing open or changed files first, warming the parser at worker start, or caching parse results.

features.description: App shell: header, three resizable and collapsible columns, tab strip, status bar.
steps: Resize and collapse both side columns; widths persist after reload
Visual snapshot matches the approved baseline
features.notes: Verified 2026-11-22 on PR #12: step 1 by the F-201 e2e tests (drag, keyboard, collapse, reload persistence; the keyboard and persistence test also runs on Firefox and WebKit as @smoke); step 2 by the @visual test against the CI-rendered baseline e2e/__screenshots__/app-shell-layout.spec.ts/app-shell-default-chromium-linux.png, viewed and approved by the orchestrator (ADR 0021).

features.description: Projects in IndexedDB: create, switch, rename, delete; autosave with saved state in the header; persistent storage request and quota warning.
steps: Create a project, edit, reload: the edit is there
Header shows saving then saved
Simulated quota at 85% shows the warning

features.description: New project dialog with Start blank and templates (Hello world, Samplesheet to MultiQC); every template is typed, documented and lint-clean; Publish docs checkbox.
steps: Create from each template; the canvas shows the expected nodes
Oracle job: every template passes `nextflow lint` and `nextflow run -stub`
Every template has doc comments on all processes and workflows, and schema descriptions for all parameters (no documentation suggestions)
features.notes: Template list depends on open question Q6.

features.description: Palette from the language pack: generic categories as accordions, search, preview badges.
steps: Every category expands and collapses; state persists
Searching `group` finds `groupTuple`
No legacy-only construct appears

features.description: Canvas renders projections: node kinds and colours, ports with labels and compact toggle, queue/value edges, typed badges, minimap, zoom and fit.
steps: Open each template and a corpus pipeline; visual snapshots per node kind match baselines
Typed processes and workflows show the `typed` badge, legacy ones none; value edges are dashed
Hovering an edge shows its type

features.description: Details pane: read-only details for every node kind; workflow summary when nothing is selected.
steps: Click each node kind in a fixture project: details show name, kind, file, ports with types and connections
Click empty canvas: workflow summary shows

features.description: Layout sidecar and ELK auto-layout in a worker; positions persist and survive re-parse.
steps: Open a project without a sidecar: nodes are laid out and the sidecar is written
Move a node, reload: same position
Rename a process through the app: its position is kept

features.description: View modes Graph, Split and Code per tab; Code is Monaco (lazy-loaded) editing the whole file via ReplaceFileText.
steps: Switch modes with the toggle and with G, S, C
Edit code in Split mode: the graph updates after a valid edit; an invalid edit shows a diagnostic and leaves the graph unchanged
Monaco is absent from the initial bundle (bundle report)

features.description: Undo and redo across all edit commands, one step per command.
steps: Make five different edits, undo five times: files are byte-identical to the start
Redo five times: back to the edited state

features.description: Add from palette by drag and drop or keyboard; a new process goes in its own module file with the flag and an include, plus a call in the current workflow.
steps: Drag Process onto the canvas: node appears; Files shows `modules/local/<name>/main.nf`; main.nf has the include and call
Focus Workflow in the palette and press Enter: node appears at viewport centre
Exported result passes `nextflow lint`

features.description: Connect and disconnect ports with type checking; invalid targets dim while dragging; mismatches produce diagnostics.
steps: Connect a Channel<Sample> output to a Sample input: code updates, no diagnostics
Connect a Path output to a Sample input: edge turns red with a diagnostic
Delete an edge: the call argument is removed and the code still parses
features.notes: From F-005 (S1): nextflow lint doesn't check a legacy tuple input's arity, so connecting to a legacy tuple input compares arity with its declaration (LA-14).

features.description: Edit popup, Configure tab for typed processes: name, description, inputs, stage, outputs, topics, directives (searchable from catalogue), script, stub. No kind control.
steps: Double-click a process: popup opens on Configure
Add an input, rename an output, add `cpus` from the directive list, Apply: one undo step, code updated, ports updated
Deprecated directives are not offered
There is no control for changing kind

features.description: Edit popup, Code tab: Monaco on the declaration only with Shiki Nextflow highlighting and inline diagnostics; Show whole file; Format; Apply disabled while invalid.
steps: Edit in Code, switch to Configure: the form reflects the edit
Introduce a syntax error: Apply is disabled and the error shows inline
Format produces the same text as the oracle formatter for that declaration

features.description: Configure forms for operator chains, channel factories, params block, output block, records, functions, includes.
steps: For each kind, change one property through the form and verify the code and lint result
Operator closures are editable in a small Monaco field

features.description: Configure tab for legacy processes with qualifier-based input and output editors; Migrate to typed shown only when a migration is available.
steps: Edit a legacy nf-core process's inputs in a local copy: code stays legacy and lint-clean
No silent migration happens on any edit

features.description: Workflow tabs: double-click a workflow node opens its canvas tab with breadcrumb; editing take or emit updates ports at every call site.
steps: Double-click ALIGN in a fixture: a tab opens with take and emit pills
Add a take: the ALIGN node in main.nf gains an input port
Breadcrumb back returns to main.nf

features.description: Operator chains: expand and collapse in place; drop an operator onto an edge to insert it into the chain.
steps: Drop `filter` onto an edge between two processes: the chain shows `filter`; code has `.filter { … }` in the right place
Expand and collapse a chain: code unchanged

features.description: Problems panel listing errors, warnings and suggestions with locations and quick fixes; status bar counts.
steps: Open a legacy fixture: suggestions are counted separately from problems
Apply a quick fix (for example `Channel.of` → `channel.of`): the suggestion disappears and one undo step reverts it
features.notes: From F-201: the status bar's suggestions count is plain text until the problems panel exists; F-309 makes it link to the panel (UX-03).

features.description: Multi-select, delete, copy and paste of nodes within and across projects.
steps: Copy two connected processes to another project: both module files and the connection come across
Delete a multi-selection: one undo step restores all

features.description: Doc comments: Configure description fields write nf-docs-format Groovydoc; both comment styles parsed; renames and deletes keep tags in step; details pane shows descriptions.
steps: Describe a process, one input and one output in Configure, Apply: the declaration has a Groovydoc block with the text, `@param` and `@return` lines
Rename the input: its `@param` tag is renamed
Open a legacy fixture using `Inputs:`/`Outputs:` lists: descriptions show in details; nothing is rewritten until edited
Docs oracle: nf-docs JSON for the result contains every description

features.description: Documentation suggestions: undocumented processes, workflows, ports and parameters, each with a quick fix that opens the right field.
steps: A fresh process from the palette shows a documentation suggestion; filling the description clears it

features.description: Import a public GitHub repo: ref resolution, tree listing, raw contents, filters, summary before and report after.
steps: Import nf-core/fetchngs at its pinned tag: file hashes match the corpus cache
The import uses at most two api.github.com requests (network log)
The report lists parse failures and legacy share

features.description: Import a private GitHub repo with a token held in memory by default; optional remember-on-device.
steps: Import from a private test repo with a fine-grained token
Reload: the token is gone unless remember was ticked
The token never appears in exports or console output

features.description: Zip import in a worker with top-level folder stripping and size limits.
steps: Import a GitHub archive zip of rnaseq-nf: same files as the GitHub import
A zip exceeding the limits is refused with a clear message
features.notes: From F-008 (S4): codeload.github.com only allows https://render.githubusercontent.com, so zip import is a file upload; no GitHub archive URL can be fetched in the browser.

features.description: Export project as zip, layout sidecar optional; untouched files equivalent to the source.
steps: Import, make one scripted edit, export: every file the edit didn't touch is equivalent to the source
Oracle: the exported project passes `nextflow lint` when the source did
Export, clear storage, import the zip: layout identical (ADR 0008 confirmation)

features.description: Imported legacy pipelines show typed badges only on typed code, suggestion counts, and the share of each workflow that is modelled.
steps: Import nf-core/rnaseq: nf-core processes carry no typed badge; status bar shows suggestions; workflow summary shows % modelled

features.description: Export all projects to one backup zip and import it back.
steps: Export all, clear storage, import the backup: every project restored with layout

features.description: Scheduled GitHub Action builds the registry snapshot: module index with meta.yml ports and typed/legacy detection, per-module bundles, plugin index and specs.
steps: Action runs on schedule and dispatch, and publishes with the site
Index size within QA-06
Spot check: nf-core/fastqc ports match its meta.yml and it is marked legacy (as of 2026-11)
features.notes: From F-008 (S4): the snapshot is the browser's only registry source (registry.nextflow.io sends no CORS headers; bundle downloads redirect to public-cr-prod.seqera.io, also without CORS). Paths under /api/v1/, module names %2F-encoded; the list endpoint lacks port metadata, so fetch each module's release. See docs/research/2026-11-22-spike-s4-cors.md.

features.description: RegistryClient with live and snapshot implementations and automatic fallback; palette shows source and age.
steps: Block the registry host in Playwright: palette still lists modules from the snapshot and says so
With live access (if S4 allowed it): palette shows live
features.notes: From F-008 (S4, 2026-11-22): the registry sends no CORS headers, so the live client can't work from the browser today; step 2 applies only if a re-run of the S4 probe (dispatch the S4 probe workflow) shows access. Delete the probe page and workflow here (ADR 0023).

features.description: Registry modules and plugins in the palette: namespace groups, process or workflow tag, search, lazy loading.
steps: Search `fastqc`: nf-core/fastqc appears under Modules
Scrolling the module list loads more without blocking input

features.description: Insert a registry module: bundle written to `modules/<ns>/<name>/`, include by name, reuse if present; warning per LA-14 when inserting legacy into typed if S1 requires it.
steps: Drop nf-core/fastqc into a typed template, connect it, export: passes `nextflow lint` (M5 exit)
Drop it again: the bundle is not duplicated
features.notes: From F-005 (S1): typed workflows may call legacy registry modules across files with no warning; tuple inputs as tuple(...), outputs by assignment (LA-14). .module-info isn't written until its checksum algorithm is verified with the oracle (ADR 0009 spike result).

steps: Add nf-schema: `nextflow.config` gains the plugin line; its functions appear in the palette

steps: Select an inserted module: details show version and upstream link
Make local copy: module moves to `modules/local/`, include updated, editing allowed

features.description: nextflow.config editor: forms for first-class scopes, generic typed forms for other scopes, Add scope, option docs in the right pane, selectors showing matched processes, unknown options kept.
steps: Set process memory and a withLabel selector through forms: code updated, lint-clean
An unknown option in an imported config is kept and flagged

features.description: nextflow_schema.json builder with groups, all parameter properties, Ajv validation, and sync with the params block.
steps: Add a param in the params block: the schema builder offers the matching entry
Change a type in the schema: a diagnostic with quick fix appears on the params block

features.notes: Requested by the maintainer on 2026-11-21.
